title: Battle of Abritus
description: Goths under Cniva destroy a Roman army and kill Emperor Decius and his son, the first Roman emperor to die in battle against a foreign enemy.

title: Byzantium recognises the Bulgarian state
description: After his defeat by Asparuh's Bulgars near the Danube delta, Emperor Constantine IV makes peace and agrees to pay tribute, the date taken as the founding of Bulgaria.

title: Battle of Pliska
description: Khan Krum traps the Byzantine army in the Balkan passes after it has sacked Pliska and kills Emperor Nikephoros I.

title: Baptism of Boris I
description: Khan Boris accepts Christianity from Constantinople and begins the conversion of his people.

title: Council of Preslav
description: An assembly makes Simeon ruler, moves the capital to Preslav and replaces Greek with Old Bulgarian in the church and state.

title: Battle of Achelous
description: Simeon I destroys a Byzantine army on the Black Sea coast, leaving Bulgaria the strongest power in the Balkans.

title: Battle of Kleidion
description: Emperor Basil II defeats the army of Tsar Samuel and is said to have blinded thousands of prisoners, and Bulgaria falls to Byzantium four years later.

title: Uprising of Asen and Peter
description: The brothers Theodore-Peter and Asen lead a revolt against Byzantine rule that restores a Bulgarian state with Tarnovo as its capital.

title: Battle of Adrianople
description: Tsar Kaloyan defeats the crusaders of the new Latin Empire and captures Emperor Baldwin I a year after the sack of Constantinople.

title: Battle of Klokotnitsa
description: Ivan Asen II defeats and captures Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus, making Bulgaria the leading power in south-eastern Europe.

title: Fall of Tarnovo
description: The Ottomans take the Bulgarian capital after a three-month siege, the central event in the conquest that begins nearly five centuries of Ottoman rule.

title: Battle of Nicopolis
description: Bayezid I defeats a crusading army of Hungarian, French and other western knights, and the last Bulgarian state at Vidin is absorbed soon after.

title: Battle of Varna
description: Murad II defeats a crusade led by Władysław III of Poland and Hungary, who is killed, ending the last serious attempt to drive the Ottomans from the Balkans.

title: Chiprovtsi uprising
description: Catholic Bulgarians rise in support of the advancing Habsburg army and are crushed, and the survivors flee across the Danube.

title: Paisius completes his Slavonic-Bulgarian History
description: The monk Paisius of Hilendar finishes a history urging Bulgarians to know their past and language, usually taken as the start of the National Revival.

title: Bulgarian Exarchate established
description: A decree of Sultan Abdülaziz creates a Bulgarian church separate from the Greek patriarchate, giving Bulgarians their first recognised national institution.

title: Vasil Levski hanged
description: The organiser of a network of secret revolutionary committees is executed by the Ottoman authorities and becomes the national hero of Bulgaria.

title: April Uprising
description: A revolt against Ottoman rule is put down with massacres such as that at Batak, and the outcry abroad leads to the Russo-Turkish War.

title: Siege of Plevna
description: Russian and Romanian forces besiege Osman Pasha for five months, and the fall of the town opens the road to Constantinople and to Bulgarian autonomy.

title: Tarnovo Constitution
description: A constituent assembly adopts the first constitution of the new principality, and Alexander of Battenberg is then elected prince.

title: Unification of Bulgaria
description: A bloodless coup in Plovdiv joins the Ottoman province of Eastern Rumelia to the Principality of Bulgaria, against the terms of the Treaty of Berlin.

title: Independence declared
description: Prince Ferdinand proclaims full independence from the Ottoman Empire and takes the title of tsar.

title: Treaty of Bucharest
description: Defeated by its former allies in the Second Balkan War, Bulgaria gives up most of Macedonia to Serbia and Greece and Southern Dobruja to Romania.

title: Treaty of Neuilly
description: The peace treaty after the First World War takes away Bulgaria's Aegean coast and other border areas, limits its army and imposes reparations.

title: Coup of 9 June
description: Army officers overthrow the agrarian government of Aleksandar Stamboliyski, who is killed days later.

title: Deportation of Bulgarian Jews halted
description: Protests by members of parliament, the Orthodox Church and citizens stop the planned deportation of Jews from Bulgaria proper, though more than 11,000 are sent to their deaths from Bulgarian-occupied Macedonia and Thrace.

title: Coup of 9 September
description: As the Red Army enters the country, the communist-led Fatherland Front seizes power, beginning 45 years of communist rule.

title: Monarchy abolished
description: A referendum held under communist control ends the monarchy, and a people's republic is proclaimed a week later.

title: Exodus of Bulgarian Turks
description: After years of forced name changes, more than 300,000 Turks leave Bulgaria for Turkey within a few months when the border is opened.

title: Fall of Todor Zhivkov
description: The party leadership removes the man who had led Bulgaria since 1954, the day after the Berlin Wall opens, and the move to multi-party elections begins.

title: Bulgaria joins the European Union
description: Bulgaria becomes a member of the European Union, three years after joining NATO.
